newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Parity talk re-emerges.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Parity talk re-emerges.

text.p: The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread saw a further compression on Thursday following a weaker than expected set of monthly and quarterly retail trade data, sparking off thoughts of the differential reaching parity.
The data saw the local 10-year bond futures contract strike a fresh record high of 93.675, taking the yield below 6.35 percent and the lowest level since the early 1980s.

Analysts believe the renewed buoyancy of U.S. Treasuries will give a positive backdrop for the local rally to continue, and further signs of weakness in the economy will stir up expectations for a monetary policy easing.
The Reserve Bank cut official interest rates to 5.0 percent on Wednesday, although so far there are mixed opinions whether this is the last in the cycle.
The U.S. market powered ahead on Wednesday amid a broad brush of buying interest, and generally kept to those levels in Tokyo trading.

The Canadian market had outperformed the U.S. on Wednesday, helped on by a stronger Canadian currency, while New Zealand debt dragged it heals against the bloc with one eye still on the fate of the N.Z. dollar.
